title: Scripture paints sin as defiling filth from the heart (Mark 7; Rev 22)
source_text: X. Porro hanc gratiae Christi efficaciam, qua peccatum in nobis destruit, ut nos vera justitia & sanctitate induat, Scriptura variis vocibus exprimit, & metaphoris pluribus adumbrat: prout etiam varie describit peccati malitiam atque turpitudinem. Primo enim Scriptura peccata considerat tanquam sordes quasdam atque immunditias, quae animam turpiter foedant atque maculant, Deoque odiosam & abominabilem reddunt, juxta illud Christi in Evangelio, Quae de homine procedunt illa sunt quae coinquinant hominem. Ab intus enim de corde hominum malae cogitationes procedunt, adulteria, fornicationes, homicidia, furta, avaritia, nequitiae, dolus, impudicitiae, oculus malus, blasphemiae, superbia, stultitia: Omnia haec mala ab intus procedunt, & coinquinant hominem. Marc. 7. Quo pertinet etiam quod legitur in Apocalypsi, Qui in sordibus est sordescat adhuc. Apoc. 22.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover this efficacy of Christ's grace, by which he destroys sin in us so that he may clothe us with true righteousness and holiness, Scripture expresses with various words and sketches with many metaphors: just as it also variously describes the malice and foulness of sin. For first Scripture considers sins as certain filth and uncleannesses, which foully soil and stain the soul and render it hateful and abominable to God, according to that of Christ in the Gospel: The things that proceed from a man are what defile a man. For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness, wickednesses, deceit, shamelessness, an evil eye, blasphemies, pride, folly: All these evils proceed from within and defile a man (Mark 7). To which also pertains what is read in the Apocalypse: Let him who is filthy be filthy still (Revelation 22).
pass_b_english: Grace's efficacy is imaged against sin's filth: what comes from the heart defiles (Mark 7).
Revelation 22 warns the filthy to stay filthy—sin as abominable uncleanness before God.
